SKAP2 expression in innate immune cells controlled the bacterial burden. SKAP2 expression in bone marrow-derived immune cells was required. Klebsiella pneumoniae stimulated reactive oxygen species (ROS) production in Skap2-/- neutrophils was abolished. This was observed in laboratory tests. The absence of SKAP2 significantly impaired the K. pneumoniae-induced phosphorylation of SFKs, Syk, and Pyk2. This suggests SKAP2 is an early component in their activation within pathogen-signaling pathways. SKAP2-dependent signaling in neutrophils is essential for K. pneumoniae-activated ROS production. This signaling is also essential for promoting bacterial clearance during infection.

These defects included poor development of arcuate nucleus neural projections. Leptin receptor (LepR) deficiency in early life led to irreversible obesity in mice. generated_summary: Mutations in the RAB23 gene cause Carpenter Syndrome. Rab23-deficient mice exhibited polysyndactyly and premature fusion of multiple sutures. In Rab23-deficient sutures, FGF10-driven FGFR1 signaling was elevated. This elevation led to an imbalance in MAPK, Hedgehog signaling, and RUNX2 expression. Mutations in the RAB23 gene cause Carpenter Syndrome. Carpenter Syndrome is characterized by multiple developmental abnormalities, including polysyndactyly and defects in skull morphogenesis. The study generated Rab23-deficient mice to understand how RAB23 regulates skull development. These mice survived until embryonic day 18.5, allowing skeletal development to be studied. 5 , and this allowed us to investigate how RAB23 regulates bone formation. Rab23-deficient mice exhibited polysyndactyly and premature fusion of multiple sutures. This premature fusion, called craniosynostosis, resulted from aberrant osteoprogenitor proliferation and elevated osteogenesis in the suture. In Rab23-deficient sutures, FGF10-driven FGFR1 signaling was elevated. This elevation led to an imbalance in MAPK, Hedgehog signaling, and RUNX2 expression. Disruption of Rab23 also led to an upregulation of Pitx2, Fgf10, and Fgfr1b expression. This upregulation contributed to the elevated FGF10-driven FGFR1 signaling. Hedgehog signaling was amplified with increased expression of GLI1. The study also observed decreased p38 and enhanced pERK1/2-RUNX2 signaling. Inhibition of elevated pERK1/2 signaling normalized osteoprogenitor proliferation. This inhibition also reduced osteogenic gene expression and prevented craniosynostosis in Rab23-deficient mice. RAB23 acts as an upstream negative regulator of both FGFR and canonical Hh-GLI1 signaling. RAB23 is also involved in the non-canonical regulation of GLI1 through pERK1/2.

The centrosome initiates the formation of new microtubules. Loss of Cep120 leads to aberrant dynein-dependent trafficking of centrosomal proteins. It also causes dispersal of centriolar satellites and defective ciliary assembly and signaling. Cep120 is preferentially enriched on daughter centrioles. This Cep120-dependent mechanism regulates the centrosome’s function in non-dividing cells. Cep120 helps maintain centrosome homeostasis by inhibiting untimely maturation of the daughter centriole. This inhibition prevents premature development of the daughter centriole. The findings define a potentially new molecular defect underlying the pathogenesis of ciliopathies. These ciliopathies include Jeune Asphyxiating Thoracic Dystrophy and Joubert syndrome.

Optimal ultrasensitivity in allosteric proteins is achieved when activation by individual sites is concerted and redundant. RNA sequencing identified novel associations between disease severity and PfEMP1 transcripts.
These associations included PfEMP1 domains and smaller sequence segments.
The RNA sequencing study confirmed all previously reported associations.
These were between expressed PfEMP1 sequences and severe disease. Confirming previous findings strengthens reliability.
These findings will inform efforts to identify vaccine targets for severe malaria.

generated_summary: Toxoplasma is an obligate intracellular parasite that replicates within a parasitophorous vacuole (PV) in mammalian cells. The PV does not fuse with any host organelles. This study examined how Toxoplasma exploits host lipid droplets (LD). Lipid droplets are fat storage organelles. Toxoplasma replication is reduced in host cells depleted of lipid droplets. Replication is also reduced with impaired triacylglycerol (TAG) lipolysis or fatty acid catabolism. Throughout Toxoplasma infection, the parasitophorous vacuole is surrounded by host lipid droplets. Toxoplasma can access lipids stored in host lipid droplets. The parasite incorporates these lipids into its own membranes and lipid droplets. Toxoplasma intercepts and internalizes host lipid droplets within the PV to access their lipids. These host LD become wrapped by an intravacuolar network of membranes (IVN). Mutant parasites with impaired IVN formation show reduced lipid uptake from host lipid droplets. Parasites lacking an IVN-localized phospholipase A2 are less efficient at salvaging lipids from host LD in the PV. This study highlights Toxoplasma's reliance on host lipid droplets for its intracellular development. The parasite is capable of scavenging neutral lipids from host LD.

generated_summary: Fasciolosis is an emerging zoonotic disease caused by liver flukes Fasciola hepatica and Fasciola gigantica. This disease is considered emerging due to increased reports of human infections. Resistance to triclabendazole, a main drug for fasciolosis, necessitates new treatments. New chemical entities and target molecules are needed to control fluke infections. Researchers screened forty flavonoid derivatives for inhibitors of Fasciola hepatica cysteine proteases. The proteases studied were FhCL3 and FhCL1, which are stage-specific enzymes. Chalcones with phenyl and naphthyl groups were identified as good cathepsin L inhibitors. These chalcones interacted with two binding sites within the active site cleft of the enzymes. One compound, C34, tightly bound to juvenile-specific FhCL3. C34 showed an IC50 of 5.6 μM against the enzyme. C34 is a slow-reversible inhibitor that interacts with the Cys-His catalytic dyad of FhCL3. C34 also interacts with key S2 and S3 pocket residues, which determine substrate specificity. C34 reduced the ability of NEJ to migrate through the gut wall and caused a loss of motility. This led to NEJ death within a week in vitro, and C34 was not cytotoxic to bovine cells. These findings open new avenues for developing novel agents to control fluke infection. The agents could also potentially control other helminthic diseases.

generated_summary: Under nitrogen deprivation, Anabaena filaments develop into a pattern of nitrogen-fixing heterocysts separated by photosynthetic vegetative cells. The coupling of gene expression fluctuations between cells along a multicellular filament in Anabaena was unknown. The study investigated HetR gene expression fluctuations, a transcription factor essential for heterocyst differentiation. Researchers used a chromosomally-encoded translational hetR-gfp fusion to track HetR expression. This fusion tests expression of the gene with all its transcription and translation start signals. Expression fluctuations of hetR in nearby Anabaena cells are coupled. This coupling has a characteristic spatial range of about two to three cells. Correlations between cells predominantly arise from intercellular molecular transfer. Cell division contributes less to these correlations. Fluctuations in hetR expression after nitrogen step-down can build up on those under nitrogen-replete conditions. This suggests continuity between fluctuations under different nitrogen conditions. Under nitrogen-rich conditions, the HetR inhibitor PatS is an essential determinant of hetR expression fluctuations. Cell-cell communication influenced by septal protein SepJ and positive HetR auto-regulation also determine these fluctuations. Proteins involved in activation, inhibition, and cell-cell communication control coupled fluctuations. These fluctuations, combined with stochasticity in gene expression, lead to a one-dimensional developmental pattern in Anabaena.

generated_summary: In fungal cells, cytokinesis requires the coordinated closure of a contractile actomyosin ring (CAR) and the synthesis of a division septum. The mechanism by which CAR proteins interact with septum synthesis enzymes to form the septum remains unclear. In fission yeast, cooperation between the paxillin homolog Pxl1 and Bgs1 is required for stable anchorage of the CAR to the plasma membrane. This cooperation is also needed for cleavage furrow formation before septation onset. Lack of Pxl1 combined with Bgs1 depletion causes failure of ring contraction. This also leads to lateral cell wall overgrowth towards the cell lumen without septum formation. Pxl1 concentration at the CAR increases during cytokinesis. This increase depends on the SH3 domain of the F-BAR protein Cdc15. Bgs1 depletion in cells with a cdc15ΔSH3 allele causes ring disassembly and septation blockage. This effect is similar to what happens in cells lacking Pxl1. The absence of Pxl1 is lethal when Cdc15 function is affected. This leads to CAR sliding and deposition of septum wall material along the cell cortex, suggesting additional functions for Pxl1 and Cdc15. CAR anchorage to the plasma membrane through Cdc15 and Pxl1, along with Bgs1 activity, are necessary for CAR maintenance and septum formation in fission yeast.

generated_summary: The intracellular parasite Toxoplasma possesses at least one gene coding for a protein containing the sterol-sensing domain (SSD). This protein is predicted to be an uncharacterized Niemann-Pick, type C1-related protein (NPC1). The protein shows significant identity to human NPC1, which is implicated in human NPC disease. The NPC1-related protein in Toxoplasma was named TgNCR1. TgNCR1 lacks endosomal targeting signals and localizes to flattened vesicles beneath the plasma membrane of Toxoplasma. When expressed in mammalian NPC1 mutant cells, TgNCR1 restores cholesterol and GM1 clearance from endo-lysosomes. Researchers genetically disrupted the NCR1 gene in Toxoplasma to clarify the role of TgNCR1. The mutant parasites were viable. Quantitative lipidomic analyses on the ΔNCR1 strain revealed normal cholesterol levels but an overaccumulation of cholesteryl esters, sphingomyelins, and ceramides. ΔNCR1 parasites also had abundant storage lipid bodies and long membranous tubules. ΔNCR1 mutant Toxoplasma generated multiple daughters per single mother cell at high frequencies, allowing fast replication in vitro. These mutants were slightly more virulent in mice than the parental strain. The data suggest that the ΔNCR1 strain lost the ability to control intracellular levels of several lipids. This resulted in stimulated lipid storage, membrane biosynthesis, and parasite division. The researchers ascribe a role for TgNCR1 in lipid homeostasis in Toxoplasma.

generated_summary: Heterochromatic homology ensures the segregation of achiasmate chromosomes during meiosis I in Drosophila melanogaster females. Achiasmate chromosomes are chromosomes without crossovers. The study investigated how heterochromatic threads and other DNA entanglements are resolved before anaphase I. Knockdown of Topoisomerase II (Top2) by RNAi caused a defect in the separation of heterochromatic regions. This defect occurred after spindle assembly during later stages of meiosis. In Top2 RNAi-expressing oocytes, heterochromatic regions of both achiasmate and chiasmate chromosomes failed to separate. This failure occurred during prometaphase I and metaphase I. Heterochromatic regions stretched into long, abnormal projections in some oocytes. Centromeres localized near the tips of these projections. Most Top2 RNAi-expressing oocytes had bipolar spindles. However, 4th chromosomes failed to move toward spindle poles during prometaphase I. Both achiasmate and chiasmate chromosomes showed defects in biorientation. Biorientation is the proper attachment of sister kinetochores to microtubules from opposite spindle poles. Embryos from Top2 RNAi-expressing females often failed to initiate mitotic divisions. Topoisomerase II is involved in resolving heterochromatic DNA entanglements during meiosis I. These entanglements must be resolved to complete meiosis.

generated_summary: Many countries where neglected tropical diseases (NTDs) are common cannot start or expand programs. These countries lack basic data for planning and advocacy. An integrated mapping approach for NTDs could save significant resources. This is true where these diseases geographically overlap. Researchers developed and field-tested an innovative integrated NTD mapping protocol. This protocol is called Integrated Threshold Mapping (ITM) Methodology. The ITM protocol determines if a disease threshold has been reached in an implementation unit. This threshold triggers public health interventions. Researchers tested the ITM protocol by comparing it to current World Health Organization (WHO) mapping methodologies. The comparison took place in one district each in Mali and Senegal. The ITM methodology reached the same conclusions as WHO methodologies for trachoma, lymphatic filariasis (LF), and soil-transmitted helminths (STH). These conclusions were about initiating public health interventions. ITM resulted in more targeted intervention recommendations for schistosomiasis. The ITM methodology was practical, feasible, and demonstrated overall cost savings. This was compared to standard, non-integrated WHO methodologies. This integrated mapping tool could help implement much-needed NTD programs. These programs are for countries where NTDs are common.

generated_summary: Proteins often perform their biological functions through collective atomic motions. Identifying collective motions related to a specific protein function from molecular dynamics trajectories is often difficult. The authors propose a new technique called 'functional mode analysis' (FMA) to detect collective motion directly related to a particular protein function. Functional mode analysis uses an ensemble of protein structures and a 'functional quantity' to describe the protein's functional state. The technique detects the collective motion maximally correlated to this functional quantity. The functional quantity can be a geometric, electrostatic, or chemical observable. It can also be any other variable relevant to protein function. FMA also estimates the motion most likely to cause a substantial change in the functional quantity. This estimation considers the given protein ensemble. This 'ensemble-weighted MCM' identifies the most probable collective motion. FMA applies two correlation measures: Pearson correlation coefficient and mutual information. Pearson correlation measures linear correlation, while mutual information assesses any kind of interdependence. The new FMA approach is demonstrated using several biomolecules. These include a polyalanine-helix, T4 lysozyme, Trp-cage, and leucine-binding protein.

generated_summary: Defects in primary cilia cause inherited human disorders called ciliopathies. These include retinitis pigmentosa and Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS). Cilium formation, maintenance, and function depend on intracellular transport systems like intraflagellar transport (IFT). The Bardet-Biedl syndrome (BBS) cargo-adaptor protein complex, or BBSome, regulates IFT. The study used the nematode C. elegans to identify new cilium-associated genes. Ciliogenesis occurs during late embryogenesis in C. elegans. Whole-organism RNA-Seq libraries helped discover a signature expression profile. This profile was highly enriched for transcripts of known ciliary proteins. From 185 candidate ciliary genes, the study identified orthologues of human MAP9, YAP, CCDC149, and RAB28. These are conserved cilium-associated components. C. elegans RAB-28 is exclusively expressed in ciliated neurons. This small GTPase dynamically associates with IFT trains. GTP-bound (activated) RAB-28 concentrates at the periciliary membrane. It undergoes bidirectional IFT in a BBSome-dependent manner. Overexpression of predicted GDP or GTP locked variants of RAB-28 perturbs cilium and sensory pore morphogenesis. It also perturbs their function. The findings present a new approach for identifying ciliary proteins. They unveil RAB28 as an IFT-associated cargo with BBSome-dependent functions at the ciliary base.

The endothelial glycocalyx-like layer is a molecular barrier lining blood vessels. This study examined how inflammatory mediators and endothelial cell pathways contribute to NS1-induced vascular leak. DENV NS1, but not West Nile virus NS1, triggers localized vascular leak in mice. This was observed in the dorsal dermis of wild-type C57BL/6 mice. Human dermal endothelial cells exposed to DENV NS1 do not produce inflammatory cytokines. Blocking these cytokines did not affect NS1-induced endothelial hyperpermeability. DENV NS1 induces vascular leak in TLR4- or TNF-α receptor-deficient mice. The leak levels were similar to those in wild-type animals. DENV NS1-induced vascular leak was blocked using inhibitors. These inhibitors target molecules involved in glycocalyx disruption. Inhibition of endothelial sialidases, cathepsin L, and heparanase prevented vascular leak. DENV NS1-induced vascular leak is independent of inflammatory cytokines. The leak is dependent on endothelial glycocalyx components. These findings suggest potential targets for novel therapeutics.

generated_summary: The pathophysiological mechanisms of leprosy are still incompletely understood. Leprosy is an urgent public health issue in Brazil. Complement receptor 1 (CR1) facilitates the entry of mycobacteria into macrophages. CR1 binds to complement fragments C3b/C4b on the bacteria. This case-control study investigated CR1 polymorphisms, gene expression, and soluble CR1 levels. The study aimed to understand CR1's role in leprosy susceptibility in Brazilian patients. Nine CR1 polymorphisms were genotyped in 213 leprosy patients and 297 controls. mRNA and soluble CR1 (sCR1) levels were measured in a subset of samples. Individuals with a common recombinant CR1 haplotype showed twice the susceptibility to leprosy. This haplotype included rs3849266*T and rs3737002*T, encoding p.1408Met of the York Yka+ antigen. Paucibacillary leprosy patients with these CR1 variants exhibited lower soluble CR1 (sCR1) levels. Lower sCR1 levels are associated with a reduced anti-inflammatory response. The most ancient CR1 haplotype increased susceptibility to the multibacillary clinical form of leprosy. This ancient haplotype included the intronic rs12034383*G allele. This allele was associated with higher CR1 gene expression, potentially increasing parasite internalization. The study suggests CR1 polymorphisms regulate mRNA and soluble CR1 levels. Haplotype-specific effects increase leprosy susceptibility, possibly by enhancing parasite phagocytosis and inflammation.

generated_summary: A general method was established for reversible and inducible gene knockout and rescue in mice. This system, named iKO, allows the target gene to be turned on and off by treating mice with doxycycline. The system minimizes embryonic lethality, developmental effects, and compensatory effects. The iKO method combines two genetically modified mouse lines. One line has a tetracycline-dependent transactivator replacing the target gene, and the other has a tetracycline-inducible cDNA inserted into a TIGRE genomic locus. The TIGRE locus provides for low basal expression and high inducibility. A method was developed to easily introduce genes into the TIGRE site of mouse embryonic stem (ES) cells. This was done using recombinase-mediated insertion. The TIGRE locus occurs infrequently in the genome. Both KO and TIGRE lines were engineered for high-throughput, large-scale, and cost-effective production of iKO mice. As a proof of concept, iKO mice were created in the apolipoprotein E (ApoE) gene. The ApoE gene allows for sensitive and quantitative phenotypic analyses. The iKO system demonstrated reversible switching of ApoE transcription and plasma cholesterol levels. It also showed reversible atherosclerosis progression and regression. These on/off switches occurred rapidly. The iKO system shows stringent regulation and is a versatile genetic system. It can incorporate other techniques and adapt to a wide range of applications. The system is applicable to any gene in any tissue.

East Asians had somewhat higher initial levels of Neanderthal ancestry than Europeans, even after accounting for selection. generated_summary: In humans, reinfections by Trypanosoma cruzi are thought to have major public health implications. Reinfections increase the risk of chronic manifestations of Chagas disease, but their frequency is not well understood. The study used stochastic agent-based models to estimate the rate of re-inoculation in humans. These models also assessed reinfection frequency during acute and chronic stages of Chagas disease. The models were fitted to epidemiological data from Argentinean rural villages. In these villages, mixed infections by different Trypanosoma cruzi genotypes reach 56% in humans. The best model predicted 0.032 annual reinfections per individual. This prediction helped explain the observed percentage of mixed infections. Most of these predicted annual reinfections, 98.4%, occur in the chronic phase of Chagas disease. The parasite Trypanosoma cruzi escapes the adaptive immune response in at least 20% of re-inoculation events. This escape happens after the primary infection. The risks of reinfection during the long chronic stage are around 14% after 5 years. The risk increases to 60% after 30 years, with most individuals reinfected 1–3 times overall. The low annual rates of reinfection are better explained by the weak efficiency of stercorarian transmission. This explanation is preferred over a highly efficient adaptive immune response. These estimates are important for vaccine development. They also help understand the higher risk of chronic disease manifestations in endemic areas.

generated_summary: Most dengue virus (DENV) infections are subclinical, but type-cross-reactive immunity can affect the outcome of subsequent infections. Subclinical means having mild or no symptoms. The mechanisms that control different clinical outcomes of DENV infection are not well understood. Blood samples were collected from school-aged Thai children who later experienced either subclinical DENV infection or developed dengue illness. Peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMC) collected before infection were stimulated with DENV in vitro. The secretion of 30 cytokines, which are immune signaling proteins, was then measured. generated_summary: Polygenic type 2 diabetes in mouse models is linked to obesity. This condition results from a combination of adipogenic and diabetogenic alleles. The study identified a candidate gene for the diabetogenic effect of a QTL called Nidd/SJL. This QTL was contributed by SJL, NON, and NZB strains in outcross populations with New Zealand Obese (NZO) mice. A critical interval of distal chromosome 4 (2.1 Mbp) was identified. This interval confers the diabetic phenotype. Analysis of 10 genes in the critical interval revealed allelic variance of Zfp69. Zfp69 encodes zinc finger domain transcription factor 69. In NZO and C57BL/6J mice, a retrotransposon (IAPLTR1a) disrupted the Zfp69 gene. This disruption led to a truncated mRNA lacking coding sequences for KRAB and Znf-C2H2 domains. The diabetogenic Zfp69SJL allele produced hyperglycaemia when combined with the B6.V-Lepob background. It also reduced gonadal fat and increased plasma and liver triglycerides. Zfp69 is the most likely candidate for the diabetogenic effect of Nidd/SJL. Retrotransposon IAPLTR1a contributes to the genetic heterogeneity of mouse strains. Expression of the transcription factor Zfp69 in adipose tissue may play a role in type 2 diabetes.

Passive transfer of convalescent human plasma shows promise as a possible treatment for HPS. However, the availability of convalescent plasma from survivors of this lethal disease is very limited. The study explored using DNA vaccine technology to produce antiviral biologics for human use. These biologics are specifically polyclonal neutralizing antibodies. Geese produce IgY and IgYΔFc, which can be purified at high concentrations from egg yolks. IgY antibodies from geese lack properties of mammalian Fc that can cause reactogenicity in humans. This protection occurred when administered post-exposure. In contrast, all hamsters receiving IgY/IgYΔFc from normal geese or no treatment developed lethal HPS. The DNA vaccine/goose platform can produce a candidate antiviral biological product. This product is capable of preventing lethal HPS when administered post-exposure.

generated_summary: New drugs are needed for Chagas disease because current medicines have toxic effects and partial efficacy. Existing treatments only target the acute phase of the disease. There is currently no drug available to treat the chronic stage of Chagas disease. Researchers optimized a whole cell-based assay for high-throughput screening. This assay helps find compounds that inhibit Trypanosoma cruzi infection in mammalian cells. A chemical library of 2000 compounds was screened. The screening used a recombinant Trypanosoma cruzi (Tulahuen strain) that expresses β-galactosidase. Three compounds, PCH1, NT1, and CX1, were selected. These compounds showed high activity against Trypanosoma cruzi and low toxicity to host cells in vitro. Each of the three compounds affects the intracellular proliferation of Trypanosoma cruzi amastigotes. They do this through a different mechanism of action. CX1 exhibits strong trypanocidal activity. This is crucial for developing drugs against the chronic stage of Chagas disease, where parasites are intracellular and quiescent. NT1 has a trypanostatic effect, inhibiting parasite growth without killing. PCH1 specifically affects parasite division. The three compounds also show high activity against intracellular Trypanosoma cruzi (Y strain). They are also active against related kinetoplastid species Leishmania major and L. amazonensis. Further characterization led to the selection of two compounds, PCH6 and CX2. These compounds, chemically related to the initial hits, have improved IC50 values of 2 nM. These IC50 values are approximately 100 times lower than those of current medicines. These findings offer new candidate molecules for developing treatments.

generated_summary: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) causes fever and severe joint and muscle pain. Chronic musculoskeletal pain persists in many CHIKV patients for months to years after initial infection. The cause of this chronic disease is poorly understood. Replicating virus is not detected in joint tissues during chronic disease. However, viral RNA is detected months after acute infection. Researchers developed a recombinant CHIKV, called CHIKV-3ʹ-Cre, to identify cells involved in chronic disease. This virus expresses Cre recombinase. CHIKV-3ʹ-Cre induced chronic disease in mice, including persistent viral RNA and chronic myositis and synovitis. Infection of tdTomato reporter mice with CHIKV-3ʹ-Cre resulted in tdTomato+ cells that persisted for at least 112 days. These persistent tdTomato+ cells were mainly myofibers and dermal and muscle fibroblasts. Treatment with an antibody against Mxra8 reduced tdTomato+ cells and chronic viral RNA. This implicates tdTomato+ cells as the reservoir of chronic viral RNA. Sorted tdTomato+ fibroblasts from skin and ankle harbored most of the persistent CHIKV RNA at chronic time points. The CHIKV-3ʹ-Cre and tdTomato reporter mouse system identifies cells that survive CHIKV infection. These cells are enriched for persistent CHIKV RNA.

The spatial patterns of Opisthorchis viverrini infection were primarily determined by environmental factors. Predictive modeling showed low risk in mountainous areas and high risk in the Mekong corridor. This study presents the first risk map of Opisthorchis viverrini infection in Champasack province. This map is crucial for spatially targeting control efforts.
